judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag or challenge the description of Sun_2022's simulation as lacking the 'electromagnetic (EM) field' qualifier. No comment addresses the methodological characterization of that citation.

The reviewer mentions 'electromagnetic simulations' only in a positive summary and does not challenge the claim about Sun_2022 or say the citation/method description is unsupported, overgeneralised, or mischaracterised.
The reviewer summary mentions the comparison with electromagnetic simulations in Sun_2022 but does not challenge the claim's description as overgeneralized or mischaracterized as required by Rule A.

The reviewer makes no mention of the frequency value '570 MHz' or any inconsistency between frequency values cited in different sections of the paper. The internal inconsistency between 570 MHz and 750 MHz is not flagged.
The report does not mention the inconsistent frequencies 570 MHz vs 750 MHz, nor does it challenge any quoted numerical value or figure caption associated with the data-fit example.
The reviewer makes no mention of the incorrect 570 MHz value or the discrepancy with the correct 750 MHz value mentioned elsewhere in the paper.
The reviewer does not comment on the visibility equation or the phase factor coefficient. No mention is made of the factor of 2π/λ vs π/λ discrepancy in Eq. (5).
There is no comment on Eq. (5), the visibility formula, or the Fourier phase factor coefficient; the reviewer raises phase-calibration discussion points but not the algebraic error in the exponent.
The reviewer does not comment on the visibility equation in Section 2.3.2 or identify the missing factor of 2 in the Fourier kernel phase coefficient.
The reviewer does not flag the contradiction between the Methods claiming all 12 baselines are jointly combined and the Results using only 3 baselines. No such internal consistency issue is raised.
The reviewer does not note any contradiction between Methods and Results about whether the N-S beam fit uses all 12 baselines or only 3 baselines, nor any stacked-likelihood inconsistency.
The reviewer discusses the N-S beam fitting model but fails to notice the contradiction regarding the number of baselines used (12 claimed in Methods vs 3 used in Results).
